Confirmed: **the handoff captures history before the current model turn starts**, so it misses context retrieved by `clanker_recall` during that turn.

- Snapshot created before model execution: [run_turn_runner.py:1752](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/hermes/gateway/run_turn_runner.py:1752).
- Snapshot includes only existing user/assistant text and excludes tool results: [gateway_context.py:53](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/hermes/agent/gateway_context.py:53).
- Recall returns evidence without adding it to the handoff snapshot: [slack_recall.py:244](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/slack_recall.py:244).
- Empty snapshot means the transfer stores only the latest request: [channel_tasks.py:30](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/channel_tasks.py:30), persisted at [service.py:268](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/service.py:268).
- Worker receives that saved request and cannot run recall because isolated tasks prohibit it: [service.py:498](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/vault/service.py:498), [slack_recall.py:56](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/runtime/slack_recall.py:56).

Thus the channel model knew M5/16GB/256GB, but the DM worker never received those facts. The channel’s “I’ve carried over” claim was unsupported.

Recommended correction: preserve bounded, authenticated recall evidence in backend-owned per-turn handoff state and include it in the durable transfer. Existing regression tests cover earlier conversation history, not same-turn `recall → vault_list` ([test_clanker_channel_tasks.py:252](/Users/tanishqpalandurkar/Projects/yyot/verification/probes/test_clanker_channel_tasks.py:252)). No edits or live actions performed.
